scene.logline: Late evening in an EdereAirah household: a parent is about to call the doctor for a feverish child and first spends two minutes getting the facts in order, so the call is faster and nothing important is forgotten.
scene.camera_grammar: Reporter point of view through the unseen membrane; still plates, no invented motion; the checklist appears as an object in the room, not as overlay text.

beats.purpose: Reporter identifies herself, EdereAirah and the Earth mirror: this is a habit people on both sides can use.

beats.beat: B2 The moment before the call
beats.purpose: Parent with phone in hand; child resting. Tension: what will the doctor ask?
Parent checks the danger signs card first — if any are present, call emergency services now, not the office line.
Parent writes: when it started, temperature and how it was taken, medicines given with dose and time, allergies, drinking and toileting, what has changed.
Parent writes the three questions they want answered before hanging up.
The clinician on the line hears a clear timeline; the call is short and calm.
Reporter: the same one-page packet exists for Earth viewers; it prepares a call, it does not replace one.

people.function: Narrates and frames; never gives medical instruction herself
Prepares the packet and makes the call
Resting, visible but not the focus; no distress imagery
Voice only; asks the questions the packet answered

product.title: Before You Call the Doctor — one-page pre-call packet
product.form: Printable one-page PDF plus fillable phone version
sections: Danger signs — call emergency services now
Temperature and how it was measured
Who I spoke to and what they said
product.content_boundary: Organises information for a call. Gives no diagnosis, dosing or treatment advice. Danger-sign wording must be taken from, and cited to, a named public health authority and reviewed by a licensed clinician before any release.
product.promise: Helps you give a clear timeline on the phone.
